The following is a faithful transcription of typed notes by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M.Cap.
? ? ? ! THE SECRET ! ? ? ? ?
In fiew of the manifold and oft' divergent conclusions drawn from this work: "Mystical City of God", it will surely not be out of place to offer here a few sug- gestions which we hope may conduce to the advantage of at least some of the many interested readers. Ist. The work itself was written from start to finish - almost constrained - in humble, very deferential, docile, even "blind" obedience to the venerable writer's both immediate and highest superiors in Church and state; and by them authoritatively and unreservedly approved. 2dly Its very bitterest enemies and most persistent opponents have from the very begin- Ging signalized themselve otherwise as enemies of faith and morals. (most outstanding among such enemies have been the jansenistic and atheistic members of the Parisian Sorbonne). 3dly. The work has been recommended by several outstanding Catholic universities and among its staunchest defenders can count Bishops, Cardinals and popes - for generation after generation since and including Innocent XI in 1686 shortly after it was first published.
